manifest.name: dsh-owui-chat2api
manifest.description: Open WebUI chat2api controller for DeepSeek Harness: runs the bundled reverse proxy, adjusts its config, and watches per-call usage from a panel inside DSH.

bundle.text:
# dsh-owui-chat2api - DSH bundle patch
# Adds the Open WebUI chat2api controller plugin row to the profile composition.
# DSH loads this on startup, so the plugin survives restarts.

- insert:
    - id: dsh-owui-chat2api
      name: dsh-owui-chat2api

readme.text: **English** | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

An adapter that exposes the models in your [Open WebUI](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui) as a standard
OpenAI-compatible `/v1` API for [DSH](https://github.com/anywhere-labs/dsh-desktop)
(DSH Desktop or the stock web UI), plus a usage dashboard that lives inside DSH.

It bundles [chat2api](https://github.com/Sozbo-Tang/openwebui-chat2api), runs it
as a local reverse proxy, and adds a control panel to the DSH web shell:
``` DeepSeek Harness (or any OpenAI-compatible client) │ standard /v1 API → http://127.0.0.1:8000 ▼ dsh-owui-chat2api (local reverse proxy, keeps its own login)

- ▶️ Start / stop the proxy from the panel
- 🩺 Environment check: is Python available, are the dependencies installed? —
  and a one-click **Install dependencies** button when they are not, so no
  terminal is needed
- ⚙️ Configure your Open WebUI URL, host and port
- 📊 Usage dashboard: today / yesterday / month / total, ranked per model with
  colorful share bars — plus a manual **price table** (per 1M tokens, cached
  tokens priced separately) that turns the stats into a cost estimate
- ⚡ Honest cache tracking: a cache-hit-rate card when the backend reports
  cached tokens, a clear note when it doesn't; estimated and failed calls are
  surfaced too
- 🪟 One engine, mounted where it belongs: in DSH Desktop the console is a
  right-sidebar dock tab beside your conversation; the web UI gets the floating
  **OWUI** pill (the desktop shell deliberately skips the pill so it never covers
  the chat)
- 🧠 One-click model and reasoning-level sync (see [Reasoning effort](#reasoning-effort-)) —
  it also drops models you deleted in Open WebUI, so the list tracks the backend
  instead of only ever growing
- 📜 Process log with error highlighting, follow mode and copy
- 🎨 Color-coded sections wi

Pick one of four ways: **A** is two clicks in the DSH UI, **B** is a single
command, **C** needs no `git`, **D** lets your DSH assistant do the whole thing.

readme.section: 🖱️ Option A — add it from the DSH plugin page (recommended)
readme.text:
DSH Desktop has a plugin manager built in: open the **Plugins** page in the
right sidebar (or the **Add plugin** control, the **+**) and paste this URL:

```text
https://github.com/Wecury/dsh-owui-chat2api#v0.10.2
```

readme.section: 🖱️ Option A — add it from the DSH plugin page (recommended)
readme.text:
Confirm, and DSH fetches the plugin, registers it in your profile and offers to
enable it. The `#v0.10.2` fragment pins the release tag — drop it to follow
`main`, or swap in the version you want. This is the same `dsh plugin add`
machinery as Option B, just without a terminal; `git` must be on PATH.

Then restart DSH and install the Python dependencies with one click (see
[Dependencies](#dependencies-)) — the panel's diagnostics card has a button for
it.

The `dsh` CLI ships a plugin manager. One command installs the plugin **and**
registers it in your profile (dependencies + bundles). Pick the profile that
matches your setup — `desktop` for DSH Desktop, `web` for the stock web UI:

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:Wecury/dsh-owui-chat2api#v0.10.2
dsh plugin --profile web add github:Wecury/dsh-owui-chat2api#v0.10.2
```

- `#v0.10.2` pins the release tag — use the version you want (omit it to
  follow `main`). The `https://github.com/...#v0.10.2` form works here too.
- Requires `git` on PATH (pnpm clones the repo). Behind a proxy? Export
  `http_proxy` / `https_proxy` first.
- Hit `[ERR_PNPM_EPERM] ... rename ..._tmp_...` on Windows? A junction left by
  an earlier manual install (Option C) is in the way — remove **only the
  link**, then run the command again:

```powershell
  cmd /c rmdir "%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\profiles\<desktop|web>\node_modules\dsh-owui-chat2api"
  ```

(`rmdir` on a junction removes the link only, never the target folder.)
- Restart DSH when it finishes. Later updates (same `--profile` as install):
  `dsh plugin --profile <desktop|web> update dsh-owui-chat2api`.

readme.section: 📦 Option C — from the release tarball (no git needed)
readme.text:
1. From [Releases](https://github.com/Wecury/dsh-owui-chat2api/releases) →
   **Assets**, download `dsh-owui-chat2api-<version>.tgz`.
   (The **Source code (zip)** button is the development tree — for
   contributing, not for installing.)
2. Unpack it into the plugins folder. The tarball extracts to a `package/`
   directory — move and rename it (`tar` ships with Windows 10+):

readme.section: 📦 Option C — from the release tarball (no git needed)
readme.text:
```powershell
   tar -xzf dsh-owui-chat2api-0.10.2.tgz
   Move-Item package "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\plugins\dsh-owui-chat2api-0.10.2"
   ```

Upgrading over a previous manual install? If
   `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\profiles\<desktop|web>\node_modules\dsh-owui-chat2api`
   already exists (an old junction), remove the link first —
   `cmd /c rmdir "<that path>"` — so the new `link:` dependency resolves to
   the new folder instead of a stale target.

readme.section: 📦 Option C — from the release tarball (no git needed)
readme.text:
3. Register the unpacked folder with the plugin manager — it writes the profile
   `package.json` (`link:` dependency + `dsh.profile.bundles`) itself, so you do not
   have to hand-edit it (`desktop` for DSH Desktop, `web` for the stock web UI):

```powershell
   dsh plugin --profile desktop add link:%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\plugins\dsh-owui-chat2api-0.10.2
   ```

readme.section: 📦 Option C — from the release tarball (no git needed)
readme.text:
Match the folder name to the version you downloaded. Hand-editing the profile
   `package.json` also works, but the manager owns that file now: it reconciles the
   profile against its own records on the next install or remove, and can revert rows
   it did not write (that is how another bundle once fell back to a stale pin).

readme.section: 🤖 Option D — let your DSH install it
readme.text:
Paste this to your DSH assistant and it will do the rest:

```text
请帮我安装 DSH 插件 dsh-owui-chat2api（GitHub 仓库 Wecury/dsh-owui-chat2api）。

步骤：
1. 执行：dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:Wecury/dsh-owui-chat2api#v0.10.2

The proxy is Python: it needs `requests` and `playwright` (plus the chromium
build playwright drives). You do **not** need a terminal for this — the panel does
it:

1. Open the panel → **Configuration** → the diagnostics card. If Python is found
   but the packages are missing, the card shows an **Install dependencies** button.
2. Click it. It runs `pip install requests playwright`, then
   `playwright install chromium`, streaming pip's output into the process log so a
   slow download is visible instead of a frozen button. On a system Python it adds
   `--user` automatically; inside a venv that flag is refused, so it is skipped
   there.
3. The card flips to **Ready** when it finishes. A proxy that was already running
   keeps its old interpreter until you stop and start it.

If Python itself is missing, install it first from
[python.org](https://www.python.org/downloads/) (that installer bundles pip) — the
panel cannot install an interpreter for you.

1. Restart DSH (after any install option above). The console appears as an
   **OWUI Console** tab in the right sidebar (DSH Desktop), or as the **OWUI**
   pill in the top-right corner (web UI).
2. Open the panel and set your Open WebUI URL (the default is a placeholder).
3. Click **Start**. The first run opens a browser window for a one-time
   sign-in; the session is reused afterwards.

| Symptom | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| Diagnostics shows **Attention** | Click **Install dependencies** in the diagnostics card (or run `pip install requests playwright` + `playwright install chromium` yourself) |
| Login fails / asks to sign in again | Click **Login** in the panel and sign in once in the window |
| Models missing from the DSH picker | Click **Sync models & reasoning levels**, then restart DSH |
| The URL is `your-open-webui.example.com` | That's the placeholder — set your real address, then Start |
| `[ERR_PNPM_EPERM] ... rename ..._tmp_...` when installing | An old junction from a previous manual install is in the way — `cmd /c rmdir "%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\profiles\<desktop|web>\node_modules\dsh-owui-chat2api"` (removes the link only), then run the install again |

Reasoning models (e.g. served behind a vLLM gateway) honour `reasoning_effort`,
so DSH's model picker shows the levels that model actually accepts (`off` means
"send no `reasoning_effort` at all").

The easiest way is the **Sync models & reasoning levels** button in the
Configuration section: it probes **each level of each model**, declares only the
levels the backend accepted, and writes a backup first. That matters because
acceptance is not a range — DeepSeek V4.1 takes low/high/xhigh/max but rejects
medium, and Qwen3.8-27B takes xhigh but rejects high — and a level the backend
rejects turns that pick into an HTTP 400. When your backend gains a model, click it
again — already-probed models hit the cache. A mapping that drifted out of date is
corrected in place. Models you deleted in Open WebUI are dropped from
`settings.yaml` on the next sync, so the list tracks the backend instead of only
ever growing.

For manual declaration or using `chat2api.py` standalone, see
[DEVELOPMENT.md](DEVELOPMENT.md).

- Your Open WebUI session (`.chrome-profile`, `token.json`, the usage database)
  stays on this machine and is excluded from git and from the package.
- The usage database and the proxy config live under `~/.dsh`, outside the
  plugin directory, so they survive plugin updates.
- The proxy listens on `127.0.0.1` only.

See [DEVELOPMENT.md](DEVELOPMENT.md) for the code layout, conventions and how
to test a change locally.

- Plugin code (outside `chat2api/`): MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).
- The bundled `chat2api/` proxy: MIT © openwebui-chat2api contributors — see
  [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) and
  [Sozbo-Tang/openwebui-chat2api](https://github.com/Sozbo-Tang/openwebui-chat2api).
[English](README.md) | **简体中文**

把 [Open WebUI](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui) 里的模型接进
[DSH](https://github.com/anywhere-labs/dsh-desktop)（DSH Desktop 或原版 web
界面均可）：一个把 Open WebUI 变成标准 OpenAI 兼容 `/v1` API 的本地反向代理，
外加一个内置在 DSH 里的用量面板。

它内置了 [chat2api](https://github.com/Sozbo-Tang/openwebui-chat2api)，以本地
反向代理的方式运行，并在 DSH 的页面里注入一个控制面板：

```
DeepSeek Harness（或任何 OpenAI 兼容客户端）
        │       标准 /v1 接口 → http://127.0.0.1:8000
        ▼
   dsh-owui-chat2api   （本地反向代理，自带登录凭据）

- ▶️ 从面板启动 / 停止代理
- 🩺 环境检查：Python 是否可用、依赖是否装好；缺依赖时诊断卡片上直接给
  **一键安装依赖**按钮，不用开终端
- ⚙️ 配置 Open WebUI 地址、主机、端口
- 📊 用量面板：今天 / 昨天 / 本月 / 累计，按模型排行，彩色份额条；附手动
  **价格表**（每百万 tokens、缓存单独计价），把统计变成成本估算
- ⚡ 诚实的缓存统计：后端上报了缓存 tokens 就显示命中率卡片，没上报就明说；
  估算调用与失败调用也会单独标出
- 🪟 一套引擎，装在哪就挂在哪：DSH Desktop 里控制台是右侧栏的停靠标签页，
  停在会话旁边；web 界面是右上角的悬浮 **OWUI** 圆标（桌面壳特意不挂 pill，
  免得挡住聊天）
- 🧠 一键同步模型与推理等级（见[推理等级](#推理等级-)）——会一并移除你在
  Open WebUI 中删掉的模型，列表跟随后端而不是只增不减
- 📜 进程日志：错误高亮、跟随最新、一键复制
- 🎨 分区配色 + 内联 Tabler 图标，跟随 DSH 深浅主题，零外部请求

四种方式任选：**A** 在 DSH 界面里点两下（推荐）、**B** 一条命令、
**C** 不需要 git、**D** 直接让 DSH 帮你装。

readme.section: 🖱️ 方式 A —— 在 DSH 插件页面里装（推荐）
readme.text:
DSH Desktop 自带插件管理器：打开右侧栏的**插件**页面（或右上角的**添加插件**
“+”按钮），把这个 URL 粘进去：

```text
https://github.com/Wecury/dsh-owui-chat2api#v0.10.2
```

确认后 DSH 会拉取插件、写进你的 profile 并提示启用。`#v0.10.2` 锁定
Release tag——去掉就跟踪 `main`，也可以换成你想要的版本。它和方式 B 走的是同一套
`dsh plugin add`，只是不用开终端；本机仍需有 `git`。

装完重启 DSH，然后到面板里点一下装 python 依赖（见
[依赖](#依赖-)）。

readme.section: ⚡ 方式 B —— 一条命令
readme.text:
`dsh` CLI 自带插件管理器，一条命令完成安装 **和** profile 注册
（依赖声明 + bundles 自动写入，不用手改 package.json）。按你的环境选
profile：DSH Desktop 用 `desktop`，原版 web 界面用 `web`：

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:Wecury/dsh-owui-chat2api#v0.10.2
dsh plugin --profile web add github:Wecury/dsh-owui-chat2api#v0.10.2
```

readme.section: ⚡ 方式 B —— 一条命令
readme.text:
- `#v0.10.2` 锁定 Release tag，换成你想要的版本（不写则跟踪 `main` 分支）。
  `https://github.com/...#v0.10.2` 这种写法在这里同样可用。
- 需要本机有 `git`（pnpm 走 git 拉取）；网络需要代理时先设
  `http_proxy` / `https_proxy` 再执行。
- Windows 下报 `[ERR_PNPM_EPERM] ... rename ..._tmp_...`？之前手动装过
  （方式 C）留下的 junction 挡路了——**只删链接本身**再重试：

```powershell
  cmd /c rmdir "%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\profiles\<desktop|web>\node_modules\dsh-owui-chat2api"
  ```

readme.section: ⚡ 方式 B —— 一条命令
readme.text:
（对 junction 用 `rmdir` 只删链接、不动目标文件夹。）
- 装完重启 DSH 即可。以后升级（`--profile` 与安装时一致）：
  `dsh plugin --profile <desktop|web> update dsh-owui-chat2api`。

readme.section: 📦 方式 C —— 从 Release 的 tgz 手动装（无需 git）
readme.text:
1. 到 [Releases](https://github.com/Wecury/dsh-owui-chat2api/releases) →
   **Assets** 下载 `dsh-owui-chat2api-<版本>.tgz`。
2. 解压到插件目录。tgz 解出来是一个 `package/` 文件夹，把它改名挪过去
   （Windows 10+ 自带 `tar` 命令）：

```powershell
   tar -xzf dsh-owui-chat2api-0.10.2.tgz
   Move-Item package "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\plugins\dsh-owui-chat2api-0.10.2"
   ```

readme.section: 📦 方式 C —— 从 Release 的 tgz 手动装（无需 git）
readme.text:
在旧的手动安装上升级？若
   `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\profiles\<desktop|web>\node_modules\dsh-owui-chat2api`
   已存在（旧 junction），先用 `cmd /c rmdir "<该路径>"` 删掉链接，让新的
   `link:` 依赖解析到新目录，而不是指向残留的旧目标。

3. 交给插件管理器注册这个目录——profile 的 `package.json`（`link:` 依赖 +
   `dsh.profile.bundles`）由它自己写，不用你手改（DSH Desktop 用 `desktop`，
   原版 web 界面用 `web`）：

```powershell
   dsh plugin --profile desktop add link:%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\plugins\dsh-owui-chat2api-0.10.2
   ```

readme.section: 📦 方式 C —— 从 Release 的 tgz 手动装（无需 git）
readme.text:
版本号、文件夹名换成你实际下载的版本即可。手改 profile 的 `package.json`
   也能用，但那个文件现在归插件管理器：它会在下一次安装/卸载时按自己的记录
   reconcile，把不是它写的行回滚掉（曾经因此把另一个插件降回旧版本 pin）。

readme.section: 🤖 方式 D —— 直接喊你的 DSH 装
readme.text:
把下面这段发给你的 DSH 助手，剩下的它来做：

```text
请帮我安装 DSH 插件 dsh-owui-chat2api（GitHub 仓库 Wecury/dsh-owui-chat2api）。

步骤：
1. 执行：dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:Wecury/dsh-owui-chat2api#v0.10.2

代理是 python 写的，需要 `requests` 和 `playwright`（以及 playwright 用的
chromium）。这一步**不用开终端**，面板会做：

1. 打开面板 → **Configuration** 区 → 诊断卡片。如果找到了 Python 但缺包，
   卡片上会出现**一键安装依赖**按钮。
2. 点它。它会依次执行 `pip install requests playwright` 和
   `playwright install chromium`，并把 pip 的输出实时打进进程日志——下载慢也能
   看见进度，而不是一个卡住的按钮。系统级 Python 会自动加 `--user`；venv 里这个
   参数会被拒绝，所以会自动跳过。
3. 装完卡片变成 **Ready**。已经在跑的代理仍然用旧解释器，重启它才会用上新装
   的包。

如果连 Python 都没有，请先从 [python.org](https://www.python.org/downloads/)
装一个（安装包自带 pip）；面板没法替你装解释器。

1. 重启 DSH（任一方式装完后）：DSH Desktop 里控制台是右侧栏的
   **OWUI Console** 标签；web 界面是右上角的 **OWUI** 圆标。
2. 打开面板，把 **Open WebUI 地址**改成你自己的（默认是占位符）。
3. 点 **Start**。第一次运行会弹出浏览器窗口，登录一次你的 Open WebUI，
   之后自动复用。

| 现象 | 处理 |
| --- | --- |
| Diagnostics 显示 **Attention** | 点诊断卡片上的**一键安装依赖**（或自己执行 `pip install requests playwright` + `playwright install chromium`） |
| 登录失败 / 提示重新登录 | 面板里点 **Login**，在弹窗里登一次即可 |
| 模型不在 DSH 模型列表里 | 配置区点 **Sync models & reasoning levels**，然后重启 DSH |
| 地址还是 `your-open-webui.example.com` | 那是占位符，改成本机实际地址再 Start |
| 安装时报 `[ERR_PNPM_EPERM] ... rename ..._tmp_...` | 旧的手动安装留下的 junction 挡路——`cmd /c rmdir "%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\profiles\<desktop|web>\node_modules\dsh-owui-chat2api"`（只删链接），然后重新执行安装命令 |

推理模型（比如 vLLM 网关后面那种）支持 `reasoning_effort`，DSH 的模型选择器
里就会出现该模型**真正接受**的那几档（`off` 表示完全不发这个参数）。

最省事：在面板配置区点一次 **Sync models & reasoning levels**。它会**逐个档位**
探测每个后端模型、只声明真正被接受的档位，并且先写一份备份。这一点很关键：
能否接受并不是连续的——DeepSeek V4.1 接受 low/high/xhigh/max 却拒绝 medium，
Qwen3.8-27B 接受 xhigh 却拒绝 high，声明了后端不认的档位，一选就 400。以后
后端上了新模型再点一次即可（已探测过的会走缓存），已经漂移的档位会被就地修正。
你在 Open WebUI 里删掉的模型，下次同步会从 `settings.yaml` 里移除，列表跟随后端
而不是只增不减。

想手动声明，或独立使用 `chat2api.py`，见 [DEVELOPMENT.md](DEVELOPMENT.md)。

- 你的 Open WebUI 登录会话（`.chrome-profile`、`token.json`、用量库）
  只保存在本机，已排除出 git 和发布包。
- 用量数据库、代理配置放在 `~/.dsh`（插件目录之外），升级插件不会丢。
- 代理默认只监听 `127.0.0.1`。
代码结构、核心约定、如何本地测试改动 → [DEVELOPMENT.md](DEVELOPMENT.md)。

- 插件本体（`chat2api/` 之外）：MIT — 见 [LICENSE](LICENSE)。
- 内置 `chat2api/` 代理：MIT © openwebui-chat2api contributors — 见
  [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) 与
  [Sozbo-Tang/openwebui-chat2api](https://github.com/Sozbo-Tang/openwebui-chat2api)。
